page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highmem-16-lssd is a network-optimized virtual machine instance configured for memory-intensive workloads requiring rapid local disk access. Built on the x86_64 CPU architecture, this instance provides 16 dedicated virtual CPUs paired with 124 GB of system memory, resulting in a high allocation of 7.75 GB of RAM per core. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs provisioned on this instance type.

A primary physical characteristic of this configuration is the inclusion of integrated high-speed local disk hardware. The machine comes bundled with 805 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity distributed across two physical drives. This local NVMe storage provides high-throughput, low-latency scratch space directly attached to the host, bypassing networked storage latencies. The instance includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating private networking or dedicated allocation for external connectivity.

In terms of qualitative cost efficiency and architectural tradeoffs, bundling 124 GB of memory with 805 GB of direct-attached NVMe storage represents a specialized resource profile. While instances with ephemeral local SSDs require operational strategies to handle non-persistent data persistence across reboots or termination events, they remove external storage network bottlenecks. The hardware ratio makes it well suited for high-throughput in-memory caching layers, transient big data processing, real-time analytics engines, and database systems requiring dense memory and high-performance local I/O.
